title: The Run That Stopped for Coffee
scene: You set out early in the morning planning to run five kilometres. A short warm-up walk becomes longer than expected, a newly noticed coffee shop provides a perfectly reasonable excuse to stop, and the run quietly turns into active recovery instead.
sceneJa: 朝早く5キロ走るつもりで外に出る。10分だけのウォームアップの散歩が少しずつ長くなり、途中で見つけたコーヒーショップに立ち寄った結果、ランニングはいつの間にか『アクティブリカバリー』へと変わっていく。

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: Since I was already there / getting a coffee seemed reasonable / especially as I had technically been exercising for twenty minutes
Since I was / already there getting a coffee / seemed reasonable especially as / I had technically been exercising for twenty minutes
Since I was already / there getting a coffee seemed / reasonable especially / as I had technically been exercising for twenty minutes
questions.explanation: The first chunk gives the situation, the second gives the decision, and the third supplies the speaker's justification.

questions.question: What does ‘I saw no reason to ...’ mean here?
options: I could not find a good reason to do it
I was physically unable to do it
Someone had told me not to do it
questions.explanation: ‘I saw no reason to ...’ means the speaker did not think there was a convincing reason to take that action.

questions.question: Why is the final sentence funny?
options: It treats protecting the coffee as if it were a valid reason not to complete the planned run
It suggests coffee is healthier than running
It reveals the speaker actually ran more than five kilometres
questions.explanation: The dry humour comes from calmly judging the abandoned run from the coffee's point of view, as if that were a serious factor in the decision.

speak: Begin with mild determination. Keep the pace relaxed through the walk and the discovery of the coffee shop. Read ‘Since I was already there’ as a perfectly sensible justification. Slow slightly at ‘By the time I finished my coffee’ as the original plan quietly disappears. Deliver the final sentence calmly, with no comic emphasis.
review: Flow: modest running plan → sensible warm-up → pleasant detour → coffee stop → increasingly reasonable self-justification → the run becomes active recovery → dry final reframe. Useful chunks: ‘since I was already there,’ ‘by the time ...,’ and ‘I saw no reason to ...’.
